title: Vegetable Fried Rice with Red Pepper, Peas and Sweetcorn
changes_from_base: Same egg fried rice method with carrot, red pepper, garlic, ginger, peas and sweetcorn stir-fried before the rice; egg cooked first, set aside and returned at the end.
summary: This follows the same egg fried rice method as our classic recipe, with the egg cooked first and set aside, then carrot, red pepper, garlic, ginger, peas and sweetcorn stir-fried before the rice goes in and the egg returns at the end.
equipment: large nonstick frying pan (28-30 cm) or carbon-steel wok

ingredients.item: cold cooked long-grain or jasmine rice (from about 200 g raw rice, cooked the day before)
fine sea salt or table salt
spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
red pepper, deseeded and cut into 1 cm dice

steps.title: Prepare Rice and Egg
steps.text: Crumble the cold rice between your fingers so no clumps remain, then beat the eggs with the salt until smooth. Using rice that's been chilled since the day before means the grains are drier and will fry rather than turn sticky.

steps.title: Cook the Egg First
steps.text: Heat the pan over high heat until very hot, add 1 tbsp of the fried-rice oil, pour in the egg and cook for 30-60 seconds, stirring occasionally, until fully set with no liquid egg left (71°C). Tip it onto the plate and set aside. Cooking it alone first stops it overcooking later and keeps the pieces soft rather than tough.

steps.title: Colour the Vegetables
steps.text: Add the extra tablespoon of oil, the carrot and red pepper, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just tender-crisp with lightly charred edges. The high heat sears the surfaces quickly, so the vegetables keep their crunch instead of turning soft.

steps.title: Add Aromatics and Peas
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the peas and sweetcorn and toss for 1 minute. Garlic and ginger burn quickly, so keeping them moving over the heat for just half a minute brings out their aroma without any bitterness.

steps.title: Fry the Rice
steps.text: Add another tablespoon of oil along with the rice, then stir-fry, pressing and tossing, for 3-5 minutes until the grains separate, heat through fully and start to jump in the pan. Pour the last tablespoon of oil around the edge of the pan, add the soy sauce to the same spot and toss to coat. This two-stage seasoning lets the soy sauce sizzle briefly on the hot metal before it's tossed through, deepening its flavour.

steps.title: Return the Egg
steps.text: Add the egg back to the pan, breaking it into small pieces as you toss, then stir in the white pepper and spring onion greens. Toss for 1 minute until piping hot throughout, checking that the centre of the rice reads 74°C. Serve immediately, while everything is at its hottest and most fragrant.

tips: Don't overcrowd the pan when the carrot and pepper go in — give them space to sear so they stay crisp rather than steaming soft.
Keep the garlic and ginger moving for only 30 seconds; left any longer over high heat they turn bitter.
Use day-old, chilled rice rather than freshly cooked — it's drier and separates properly in the pan instead of clumping.
Cook the egg first and set it aside so it doesn't overcook while the vegetables are frying.
safety: Check the centre of the rice reaches 74°C with a thermometer before serving, especially since it's been through several stages in the pan.
storage: Cool freshly fried rice quickly by spreading it on a tray, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours. Reheat only once, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
